title: Choreography vs Orchestration
description: Compare choreography and orchestration approaches for implementing Saga patterns.

data.text: Sagas can be implemented using choreography or orchestration. Netflix, Amazon, and Uber use both depending on the complexity of the transaction. Understanding the trade-offs helps you choose the right approach for your use case.

In orchestration, a central saga orchestrator controls the flow. It tells each service what to do and when. The orchestrator knows the entire transaction flow and handles compensation if something fails. This is similar to a conductor leading an orchestra.

In choreography, there is no central coordinator. Services publish events when they complete their work, and other services react to those events. Each service knows only its part of the flow. This is like dancers following a shared rhythm without a conductor.

data.title: Orchestration vs Choreography Comparison
items: Orchestration: Central control, clear flow, easier to debug, single point of failure
Choreography: Decentralized, more flexible, harder to trace, no single point of failure
Orchestration is better for complex flows with many steps
Choreography is better for simple, decoupled flows

data.title: Example: Order Saga Comparison
data.code:
# Orchestration
# Order Saga Orchestrator:
# Step 1: Call Order Service -> Create Order
# Step 2: Call Inventory Service -> Reserve Stock
# Step 3: Call Payment Service -> Charge Customer
# Step 4: Call Shipping Service -> Create Shipment
# If Step 3 fails: Compensate Steps 2, 1

# Choreography
# Order Service -> OrderCreated event
# Inventory Service listens -> ReserveStock event
# Payment Service listens -> PaymentProcessed event
# Shipping Service listens -> ShipmentCreated event
# If Payment fails -> PaymentFailed event
# Inventory Service listens -> ReleaseStock event

data.caption: Orchestration vs choreography
data.definition:
graph LR
    subgraph Orchestration
        O[Orchestrator] --> S1[Service 1]
        O --> S2[Service 2]
        O --> S3[Service 3]
    end
    subgraph Choreography
        E1[Event 1] --> S4[Service 4]
        S4 --> E2[Event 2]
        E2 --> S5[Service 5]
        S5 --> E3[Event 3]
        E3 --> S6[Service 6]
    end

items.question: Which should I choose?
items.answer: Start with choreography for simple flows. Move to orchestration when the flow becomes complex and hard to trace. Many systems use both.

items.question: Can I mix both patterns?
items.answer: Yes. Use choreography for simple, decoupled workflows. Use orchestration for complex business processes that require clear error handling and compensation.

items.question: How do I monitor sagas?
items.answer: Use distributed tracing to follow saga execution across services. In orchestration, monitor the orchestrator. In choreography, track events in the message broker.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Orchestration uses a central coordinator; choreography uses events
Orchestration is clearer for complex flows
Choreography is more decoupled but harder to trace
data.takeaway: Choose based on flow complexity; start simple and evolve as needed.
